title: Transcript of Special briefing by MEA (April 23, 2025)
notes: CCS decisions: Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, ICP Attari closed, SVES visas cancelled, defence advisers declared persona non grata, High Commission strength 55→30. Content confirmed via search excerpt and PIB 14 May backgrounder.

title: Transcript of Special Briefing on OPERATION SINDOOR (May 07, 2025)
notes: FS Vikram Misri, Col Sofiya Qureshi, Wg Cdr Vyomika Singh. Strike window 01:05–01:30 IST; nine camps named with attributed organisations and stated distances from LoC/IB.

title: Operation SINDOOR: Indian Armed Forces carried out precision strike at terrorist camps
notes: Nine sites targeted; 'focused, measured and non-escalatory'; no Pakistani military facilities targeted. Content confirmed via search excerpt (direct fetch blocked).

title: Pakistan's bid to escalate negated – proportionate response by India
notes: Fifteen Indian locations named as attempted targets on night of 7–8 May; Integrated Counter UAS Grid; Lahore AD system neutralised; LoC shelling sectors; 16 civilians killed incl. 3 women and 5 children.

title: Transcript of Special briefing on OPERATION SINDOOR (May 08, 2025)
notes: Same locations as PIB 8 May; 16 civilians killed and 59 injured (search excerpt). Poonch Gurdwara attack referenced in 9 May briefing.

title: Transcript of Special briefing on OPERATION SINDOOR (May 09, 2025)
notes: 300–400 drones at 36 locations Leh–Sir Creek; preliminary ID Asisguard Songar; armed UAV at Bathinda neutralised; Indian armed drones at four Pakistani AD sites, one AD radar destroyed; shelling Tangdhar, Uri, Poonch, Mendhar, Rajouri, Akhnoor, Udhampur; Pakistan civil airspace not closed; Poonch Christ School and convent hit by shelling on 7 May.

title: Transcript of Special briefing on OPERATION SINDOOR (May 10, 2025) – morning
notes: 26+ locations Srinagar–Naliya; limited damage at IAF stations Udhampur, Pathankot, Adampur, Bhuj; high-speed missiles after 01:40 at Punjab air bases; Indian strikes on Rafiqui, Murid, Chaklala, Rahim Yar Khan, Sukkur, Chunian (air-launched precision weapons) and radar sites Pasrur, Sialkot aviation base; rebuttal of claims re S-400 Adampur, Suratgarh, Sirsa, BrahMos Nagrota; Rajouri ADDC killed.

title: Statement by Foreign Secretary (May 10, 2025) – DGMO understanding
notes: Pakistan DGMO called Indian DGMO at 15:35 IST; cessation of firing and military action on land, air and sea from 17:00 IST; DGMOs to talk again 12 May at 12:00.

title: Transcript of Special briefing by MOD on OPERATION SINDOOR (May 10, 2025) – evening
publisher: Ministry of External Affairs / Ministry of Defence
notes: Cmde Raghu R Nair, Col Qureshi, Wg Cdr Singh. Rebuttal of Pakistani claims (S-400, BrahMos, airfields Srinagar/Jammu/Pathankot/Bhuj/Naliya, ammunition depots Chandigarh/Beas); extensive damage claimed at Skardu, Sargodha, Jacobabad, Bholari; loss of Pakistani AD systems and radars.

title: Statement by Foreign Secretary (May 10, 2025) – violations of understanding
notes: Repeated violations of the DGMO understanding 'over the last few hours'; armed forces responding; instructions to deal strongly with repetition. Clock time of statement not given in transcript.

title: Event Detail: DGMO and service representatives brief media on Operation Sindoor (11 May 2025)
notes: Photo record of briefing by Lt Gen Rajiv Ghai (DGMO), Air Marshal AK Bharti (DGAO), Vice Adm AN Pramod, Maj Gen SS Sharda. No official transcript found online; the briefing content is cited from the PTI wire report (SRC-MED-PTI-0511).

title: India inflicted heavy losses on Pakistan military: Armed Forces
notes: Wire report of the 11 May tri-service briefing (DGMO Lt Gen Rajiv Ghai, DGAO Air Marshal AK Bharti, DGNO Vice Adm AN Pramod). Reports: 35–40 Pakistani military fatalities ('reports of'), five Indian military personnel killed, losses acknowledged without detail, 'a few' Pakistani planes downed. Media report of Indian official statements; no official transcript located.

title: Operation SINDOOR: India's Strategic Clarity and Calculated Force
publisher: Press Information Bureau (Ministry of Information & Broadcasting)
notes: Rafale, SCALP and HAMMER named; mission 'in just 23 minutes'; 100+ terrorists killed; Yusuf Azhar, Abdul Malik Rauf, Mudassir Ahmad named; '11 airbases' and '20% of Pakistan's air force assets' claims; radar near Gujranwala; Bholari casualties; post-ceasefire drone waves.

title: Operation SINDOOR: The Rise of Aatmanirbhar Innovation in National Security
publisher: Press Information Bureau (Ministry of Information & Broadcasting)
notes: AD systems used: Pechora, OSA-AK, LLAD guns, Akash; IACCS; loitering munitions against radar and missile systems; debris: PL-15, Turkish 'Yiha' UAVs, long-range rockets, quadcopters, commercial drones; DGMO 12 May layered C-UAS / EW / AD description.

title: Forging One Force: The Synergy of India's Armed Forces
notes: Tri-service account; Nur Khan and Rahimyar Khan named; Akash, Pechora, OSA-AK; Army AD: MANPADS, LLAD guns, long-range SAMs; Navy CBG with MiG-29K and AEW helicopters; BSF foiled infiltration in Samba (at least two infiltrators neutralised).

title: Akashteer: The Unseen Force Behind India's New War Capability
notes: PIB backgrounder (Ministry of I&B), 16 May 2025, 17:54. Describes Akashteer as the Army's indigenous automated AD control and reporting system, integrated with IACCS (IAF) and TRIGUN (Navy), credited with countering the 9–10 May attack. Promotional in tone; capability claims are not operational detail.

title: English rendering of PM's address to the Nation (May 12, 2025)
notes: Key points summarised in PIB 14 May backgrounder: response to terror attacks, no tolerance of nuclear blackmail, no distinction between sponsors and terrorists.

title: Ministry of Defence: Year End Review – 2025
notes: MoD Year End Review 2025 (PIB, 31 Dec 2025, 16:25). Operation Sindoor section: nine camps, over 100 terrorists killed; Pakistan's attack of 10 May 'at approx. 1:30 am'; airbases struck include Chaklala, Sargodha, Rafiqui, Rahimyar Khan, Jacobabad, Sukkur and Bholari; DGMO call 10 May; formal DGMO talks 12 May.

title: UN Security Council press statement on the Pahalgam terrorist attack (25 April 2025), as quoted by MEA
publisher: United Nations Security Council (quoted in MEA 7 May briefing)
notes: The UNSC condemned the attack and called for perpetrators, organisers, financiers and sponsors to be held accountable. Quoted second-hand in the MEA transcript; the UN press release itself was not retrieved.

title: OpenStreetMap Nominatim gazetteer – Sarjal (node 8917828735), Kotli Bhatta (node 3736878071), Gulpur (node 2816160080)
notes: Village/town positions only (accessed 7 Nov 2026). Corroborates where a named place is – not that a strike occurred or what it hit. Positions checked against briefers' stated distances from the LoC/IB.

title: Operation Sindoor: JeM's communication network concealed in Pakistan's Sarjal destroyed
notes: Places the facility in a primary health centre in Tehra Kalan village, Sarjal (Narowal district). Lead paragraph read on the live page; the Internet Archive capture holds only the page shell.

title: All you need to know about the 9 terror hideouts targeted by India in Operation Sindoor
notes: Places Mehmoona Joya in the Head Marala area of Sialkot, within the Bhutta Kotli Government Basic Health Unit premises. Read via search excerpt.

title: Four Days in May: The India-Pakistan Crisis of 2025
notes: Independent early assessment drawing on commercial satellite imagery: attacks confirmed at most named Pakistani air bases; runways cratered at Sargodha and Rahim Yar Khan; hangars hit at Sukkur, Bholari, Jacobabad; no commercial imagery known for Chunian, Pasrur, Rafiqui; overwhelming evidence of the 8 May Lahore AD strike; no imagery showing meaningful damage at Indian facilities.

title: Inside Muridke: Did India hit a 'terror base' or a mosque?
notes: Reporter at the Muridke compound hours after the strike: administrative block and mosque hit, roof collapse and holes, three clerical staff killed; compound founded by Hafiz Saeed (JuD/LeT).

title: Indian strikes on Pakistan damaged six airfields, Post analysis finds
notes: Imogen Piper, Evan Hill, Maham Javaid and Rick Noack (title and authors as cited by Stimson, note 70). Paywalled; only the headline finding is used. Base-level details are not taken from this source.

title: India and Pakistan Talked Big, but Satellite Imagery Shows Limited Damage
notes: Agnes Chang, Pablo Robles and Mujib Mashal (as cited by Stimson, note 70). Not retrieved (paywalled). Listed in the imagery register by headline only; no finding is taken from it.

title: Clear satellite pics show extensive damage to Pak bases after Indian strikes
notes: Subham Tiwari and Bidisha Saha. Publishes Maxar Technologies imagery collected on 10 and 11 May of Sukkur, Nur Khan, Rahim Yar Khan, Sargodha (Mushaf), Jacobabad and Bholari. Only the opening was readable. The imagery is commercial; the 'extensive damage' reading is the outlet's.

title: Fresh satellite images reveal extent of damage at Nur Khan airbase, Pakistan takes down damaged structures
notes: Javaria Rana. Reports imagery dated 23 May shared by OSINT analyst Damien Symon (The Intel Lab) showing a complex near the Nur Khan strike site had been demolished. Partial paywall; the opening paragraphs were read.

title: India top general admits aerial 'losses' in recent conflict with Pakistan
notes: Reports Gen Anil Chauhan (CDS) acknowledging initial aerial losses without numbers and calling Pakistan's claim of five jets 'absolutely incorrect'; also notes Islamabad acknowledged its air bases suffered some hits.

title: India says six Pakistani aircraft shot down during May conflict
notes: Reports Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh claiming five Pakistani fighters and one large aircraft shot down, mostly by S-400; Pakistan rejects the claim.

title: Pakistan downs 5 Indian jets as retaliation for late-night strikes at 6 sites: officials
notes: Pakistani military account of the 7 May strikes: six sites with strikes, casualties and damage per site; claim of five Indian jets downed. Publication date as shown (US time).

title: Now you just wait for our response, DG ISPR warns India
notes: DG ISPR: India targeted Nur Khan, Murid and Shorkot air bases with air-to-surface missiles; says all air force assets are safe and most missiles were intercepted.

title: Marka-e-Haq: 40 civilians, 11 personnel of armed forces embraced martyrdom
notes: ISPR: 40 civilians (7 women, 15 children) killed and 121 injured on the night of 6–7 May; 11 armed forces personnel killed (6 Army, 5 Air Force, incl. Sqn Ldr Usman Yousuf) and 78 wounded.
